title: SARUAV convolutional-network detector locates an unconscious 65-year-old in tall grass during a Bieszczady Mountain Rescue search
summary: 29 June 2021: SARUAV CNN flagged a 65-year-old man unconscious in tall grass after 24+ h; GOPR Bieszczady retrieved him alive
account: On Monday 28 June 2021 at about 4 pm a 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's disease left his home in Cergowa, south-east Poland. He had a stroke the previous day. Police and tracking dogs did not find him after a storm. On Tuesday 29 June the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service (GOPR Bieszczady) flew four drone flights. It ran SARUAV, software from University of Wrocław researchers that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to find people in nadir aerial images, on 782 images. After 4 h 31 min of analysis the system detected him and returned his coordinates. He was lying unconscious in grass over two meters tall after more than 24 hours outdoors. GOPR rescuers carried him out and handed him to the ambulance service. The original study explicitly dates the search and rescue operation to June 29, 2021.
purpose: Built to detect people automatically in drone imagery for search and rescue; this benefit is that purpose.
system: SARUAV (Search and Rescue with Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) human detection software
model_version: SARUAV, run on images from DJI Matrice 300 drones
developer: SARUAV Ltd. / University of Wrocław (team of Tomasz Niedzielski)

ratings.reason: A 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's and a stroke a day earlier lay unconscious in two-meter grass after over 24 hours outdoors. He was found and handed to the ambulance service alive.
GOPR Bieszczady closed a search that police, dogs and ground teams had not resolved, in what it called the first such find in Poland.

ai_role.statement: The CNN detector returned the man's coordinates after police and tracking dogs had failed. Rescuers then retrieved him. Three of the five case-report authors work for SARUAV Ltd., so the independent confirmation is the GOPR Bieszczady account quoted in the Polish press.

fields.account: On Monday 28 June 2021 at about 4 pm a 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's disease left his home in Cergowa, south-east Poland. He had a stroke the previous day. Police and tracking dogs did not find him after a storm. On Tuesday 29 June the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service (GOPR Bieszczady) flew four drone flights. It ran SARUAV, software from University of Wrocław researchers that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to find people in nadir aerial images, on 782 images. After 4 h 31 min of analysis the system detected him and returned his coordinates. He was lying unconscious in grass over two meters tall after more than 24 hours outdoors. GOPR rescuers carried him out and handed him to the ambulance service. The original study explicitly dates the search and rescue operation to June 29, 2021.

fields.title: SARUAV convolutional-network detector locates an unconscious 65-year-old in tall grass during a Bieszczady Mountain Rescue search
fields.headline: SARUAV finds an unconscious 65-year-old alive in tall grass

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.

fields.account: On Monday 28 June 2021 at about 4 pm a 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's disease left his home in Cergowa, south-east Poland. He had a stroke the previous day. Police and tracking dogs did not find him after a storm. On Tuesday 29 June the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service (GOPR Bieszczady) flew four drone flights. It ran SARUAV, software from University of Wrocław researchers that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to find people in nadir aerial images, on 782 images. After 4 h 31 min of analysis the system detected him and returned his coordinates. He was lying unconscious in grass over two meters tall after more than 24 hours outdoors. GOPR rescuers carried him out and handed him to the ambulance service. The original study explicitly dates the search and rescue operation to June 29, 2021.
